conflicts_in.fact: Direction of the UGX-per-KES conversion rule and which rate applies when Amina hands over KES. The lessons contradict standard bureau practice and also disagree internally on rule wording.
conflicts_in.versions: Lesson 7 Learned says 'use the selling rate' to convert KES to foreign currency, then says for UGX-per-KES rates multiply by the buying rate. Lesson 7 Explained says the buying rate is less favourable to Amina. Lesson 8 says 28.50 instead of 27.80 would be an error, and that the buying rate applies when Amina hands over KES. The sequence says 'selling rate to get foreign currency' but applies the buying rate, so the stated rule and the applied rate conflict.

conflicts_in.fact: Who handles the Uganda transfer and how it is charged. Lesson 4 has the transfer charged only a 3% commission with no exchange rate step, while Lesson 7 places the transfer at a Kondele agent applying both 3% commission and a forex spread, and Lesson 4 locates the agent in Kericho.
conflicts_in.versions: Lesson 4: a Kericho M-PESA agent charges 3% on KSh 1,140, and the aunt receives KSh 1,105.80 (in KSh). Lesson 4 predict scene: Amina goes to a kiosk near Kondele, and the aunt receives KSh 1,106. Lesson 7: the Kondele mobile-money agent deducts 3% and also converts at the buying rate, and the aunt gets UGX 30,741.

conflicts_in.fact: Amina's mandazi weekly costs and sales, and the profit used to explain her KSh 4,500 savings.
conflicts_in.versions: Lesson 5: Amina earns weekly revenue KSh 2,250 on KSh 1,800 costs (profit KSh 450). Lesson 6 Explained: her KSh 4,500 came from two weeks of revenue of KSh 2,250, yet profit is only KSh 450 a week, so two weeks of profit is KSh 900, not KSh 4,500. Lesson 6 Model Building treats revenue (KSh 4,500 = 2 x 2,250) as her savings, ignoring the KSh 1,800 weekly cost.
